title: Krichevsky–Trofimov wealth for bounded real coins

source.author: Francesco Orabona
source.title: Online Learning: A Modern Introduction Using Convex Optimization

anchors.name: Theorem 13.4 and equation (13.1), wealth induction and exponential lower bound

inventory.effective_statement: For arbitrary c_t in[-1,1], initial epsilon>0, KT beta_t=sum_{i<t}c_i/t and wealth update W_t=W_(t-1)(1+beta_t c_t) satisfy W_T>=epsilon*2^T*Gamma((T+1+sum c)/2)*Gamma((T+1-sum c)/2)/(pi Gamma(T+1))>=epsilon exp((sum c)^2/(2T)-(ln T)/2-1).
inventory.raw_row_hash_method: SHA-256 of the UTF-8 JSON object token, from its opening brace through its matching closing brace in the original inventory bytes, without adjacent indentation, comma or newline.
inventory.canonical_row_hash_method: UTF-8 JSON with sorted keys, unescaped Unicode and no whitespace outside strings.

indexing.prefix: ktPrefix c n = ∑ i<n, c i. It excludes c n and is zero for n=0.
indexing.bet_and_update: At source round n+1, β=ktPrefix c n/(n+1) and W_(n+1)=W_n(1+c n·β). Wealth starts at ε>0.
indexing.quantified_space: Coins, wealth and potential arguments are real scalars. Time indices are natural numbers.

potential.name: BanditRL.OnlineKT.ktPotential
potential.definition:
noncomputable def ktPotential (ε : ℝ) (t : ℕ) (x : ℝ) : ℝ :=
  ε * (2 : ℝ)^t * Real.Gamma (((t : ℝ) + 1 + x) / 2) *
    Real.Gamma (((t : ℝ) + 1 - x) / 2) /
      (Real.pi * Real.Gamma ((t : ℝ) + 1))
potential.source_domain: The book uses F_t on [−t,t]. Lean defines the displayed real expression everywhere, and the named inequalities impose the printed domains.

definitions.name: ktPrefix
definitions.text:
def ktPrefix (c : ℕ → ℝ) (n : ℕ) : ℝ :=
  ∑ i ∈ range n, c i

definitions.name: ktWealth
definitions.text:
def ktWealth (ε : ℝ) (c : ℕ → ℝ) : ℕ → ℝ
  | 0 => ε
  | n + 1 => ktWealth ε c n * (1 + c n * ktPrefix c n / ((n : ℝ) + 1))

theorem_headers.name: ktPotential_interpolate
theorem_headers.header:
theorem ktPotential_interpolate (ε : ℝ) (hε : 0 < ε) (t : ℕ) (ht : 1 ≤ t)
    (x c : ℝ) (hx : |x| ≤ (t : ℝ) - 1) (hc : |c| ≤ 1) :
  ktPotential ε t (x + c) ≤ (1 + c * x / (t : ℝ)) * ktPotential ε (t - 1) x
theorem_headers.meaning: Equation (13.1). For t≥1 and |x|≤t−1, the next potential is bounded by the previous potential times 1+cx/t for every real c∈[−1,1]. This includes c=±1 and |x|=t−1. For t=1 the prior sum is x=0. The multiplier is at least 1/t>0.

theorem_headers.name: ktPrefix_succ
theorem_headers.header:
theorem ktPrefix_succ (c : ℕ → ℝ) (n : ℕ) :
  ktPrefix c (n + 1) = ktPrefix c n + c n
theorem_headers.meaning: Finite-sum bookkeeping. The prefix of n+1 coins adds c n to the prefix of n coins. This identity needs no bound on c, including when n=0.

theorem_headers.name: ktPotential_le_wealth
theorem_headers.header:
theorem ktPotential_le_wealth (ε : ℝ) (hε : 0 < ε) (c : ℕ → ℝ) (n : ℕ)
    (hc : ∀ i < n, |c i| ≤ 1) :
  ktPotential ε n (ktPrefix c n) ≤ ktWealth ε c n
theorem_headers.meaning: First wealth bound at every n≥0. Only i<n coins are bounded; the next and future coins are arbitrary. At n=0 the sum is empty and both potential and wealth equal ε.

theorem_headers.name: ktPotential_exp_lower
theorem_headers.header:
theorem ktPotential_exp_lower (ε : ℝ) (hε : 0 < ε) (n : ℕ) (hn : 1 ≤ n)
    (x : ℝ) (hx : |x| ≤ (n : ℝ)) :
  ε * Real.exp (x^2 / (2 * (n : ℝ)) - Real.log (n : ℝ) / 2 - 1) ≤ ktPotential ε n x
theorem_headers.meaning: Second bound at every n≥1 and every |x|≤n, including x=±n. The final cost is log(n)/2+1. The two simplex masses (n+x)/2 and (n−x)/2 are nonnegative and may vanish.

theorem_headers.name: ktWealth_two_step
theorem_headers.header:
theorem ktWealth_two_step (ε : ℝ) (hε : 0 < ε) (c : ℕ → ℝ) (T : ℕ) (hT : 1 ≤ T)
    (hc : ∀ i < T, |c i| ≤ 1) :
  ktPotential ε T (ktPrefix c T) ≤ ktWealth ε c T ∧
  ε * Real.exp ((ktPrefix c T)^2 / (2 * (T : ℝ)) - Real.log (T : ℝ) / 2 - 1) ≤
    ktPotential ε T (ktPrefix c T)
theorem_headers.meaning: Theorem 13.4. For every T≥1 and real coin sequence bounded only at i<T, both inequalities hold at the same S_T: F_T(S_T)≤W_T and ε exp(S_T²/(2T)−log(T)/2−1)≤F_T(S_T).

source_and_candidate_routes.printed: Equation (13.1) uses convexity of log F_t(x+c)−log(1+cx/t) on the closed coin interval and the two endpoint equalities. Wealth induction then yields the first bound. A.13, the closed binary KL lower bound and the dimension-two Gamma ratio yield the second bound.
source_and_candidate_routes.candidate_interpolation: The candidate applies convexity separately to both log-Gamma terms, uses convexity of exp, and substitutes the same two endpoint equalities. This is an alternative proof of equation (13.1).
source_and_candidate_routes.candidate_exponential_bound: Take the logarithm of the actual two-coordinate simplex product. Zero masses use the closed log-product identity and weighted zero-log terms. The two dimension-two ratio conjuncts preserve the final −1.
